assessments.reasoning: Authenticity follows from publisher_live at Creative Commons' zero/1.0/legalcode.txt. Integrity follows from its scoped full-body digest, the identical publisher_pin digest and the matching [5884,6024) citation digest. Relevance is direct because those bytes contain section 4(a). Interpretation follows its express exclusion of both trademark and patent rights from waiver and license. Applicability follows from “held by Affirmer” and “by this document,” read with the Statement of Purpose defining the Affirmer who applies CC0. The contradiction check against sections 1(iv), 2, 3 and 4(c) confirms the exclusion in both operative mechanisms and distinguishes rights held by others.

challenge.method: Tested the breadth of the waiver, the fallback license and its residual nonassertion language separately against section 4(a). Checked whether the unfair-competition provision or the discussion of other persons' rights enlarged their scope.
challenge.results: Section 1(iv) expressly subjects unfair-competition rights to 4(a). The section 2 waiver and section 3 fallback each concern Copyright and Related Rights, including the residual undertaking in section 3. Section 4(a) expressly covers licensing as well as waiver. Section 4(c) addresses third-party clearance separately.

limitations: The finding concerns the effect of applying this instrument to a Work and the patent and trademark rights the Affirmer holds.
Section 4(c) disclaims responsibility for clearing other persons' rights. Separate grants, defenses, ownership and third-party permissions require their own evidence.
reasoning: Section 4(a) expressly preserves trademark and patent rights “held by Affirmer” against waiver, surrender, licensing or any other effect of this document. Section 2 waives the Affirmer's Copyright and Related Rights to the extent permitted by law. Section 3 licenses those same rights to the extent the waiver is judged ineffective. The exclusion therefore holds under either mechanism.
